slides.say: A B C D is a parallelogram. Given: A B is ten centimeters, B C is fourteen centimeters, and angle A B C is one hundred fifty degrees. What is the area of the parallelogram, in square centimeters?
at: A B C D is a parallelogram

slides.say: The area of a parallelogram is base times height. The base B C is fourteen, so we need the height to B C. [short pause] Angle B is obtuse, so first we need to see where that height falls.
[short pause] Here's the base, B C, fourteen. Angle B is obtuse, so A is to the left of B. The perpendicular from A would land left of B, outside the segment B C.
So first we start at B and extend C B beyond B. Now we draw the perpendicular from A to that line, and call its foot H.
at: So first we start at B

slides.say: Angle A B H and angle A B C sit together on one straight line, so angle A B H is one hundred eighty minus one hundred fifty, which is thirty.
at: so angle A B H is

slides.say: Triangle A B H has a right angle and a thirty degree angle, so it's a gold triangle, thirty, sixty, ninety. A B is its hypotenuse, ten. The height A H is across from the thirty, so it's the short leg, and the short leg is half the hypotenuse. Half of ten is five.

Careful, the long leg is B H, five root three, and it isn't the height. That's where seventy root three, choice number two, comes from. And the height is five, not the slanted side ten. Fourteen times ten, a hundred forty, is choice number one, another trap.
at: Fourteen times ten, a hundred forty

slides.say: Now the area of the whole parallelogram, base times height. The base is B C, fourteen, and the height to it is A H, five. Fourteen times five is seventy. We don't divide by two, because it's a parallelogram, not a triangle. Thirty-five, choice number four, is that trap. Choice number three is our answer.
at: Now the area of the whole parallelogram
Choice number three is our answer

slides.say: So here's the rule. When the slanted side meets the base at thirty or at a hundred fifty degrees, the height to that base is half the slanted side. Here A B meets the line of B C at a hundred fifty, so A H is half of A B. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
